source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Urine output below 400 mL/24 h with rising potassium marks which phase of acute renal failure?
questions.rationale: Oliguric phase: <400 mL/day, hyperkalemia, acidosis, fluid overload.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Phases of ARF (PDF p. 388)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During the diuretic phase of acute renal failure, the nurse watches for:
questions.rationale: Output of 3–5 L/day can cause hypokalemia and volume depletion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Phases of ARF (PDF p. 388)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Kayexalate is given in renal failure to:
questions.rationale: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate exchanges sodium for potassium in the gut.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ARF Management (PDF p. 389)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diet suits a client in oliguric acute renal failure?
questions.rationale: Moderate protein restriction, high carbohydrates, restricted potassium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ARF Nursing (PDF p. 389)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the leading cause of chronic renal failure?
questions.rationale: Diabetes, then hypertension and glomerulonephritis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chronic Renal Failure (PDF p. 389)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: End-stage renal disease (CKD stage 5) corresponds to a GFR below:
questions.rationale: Stage 5 (ESRD) is GFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m².
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CKD Stages (PDF p. 389)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: White crystals on the skin of a client with ESRD are called:
questions.rationale: Uremic frost is urea crystallized on the skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CRF Manifestations (PDF p. 390)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Anemia in chronic renal failure is mainly due to:
questions.rationale: Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin; it is replaced pharmacologically.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CRF Management (PDF p. 390)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Daily fluid allowance in CRF is usually the previous day's urine output plus:
questions.rationale: Allow 500–600 mL more than the previous 24-hour output to cover insensible losses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CRF Nutrition (PDF p. 391)
questions.quote: Fluid allowance (500-600Ml) more than the previous days 24 hour urine output

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which protein source is preferred for a client with CRF?
questions.rationale: Allow limited protein of high biologic value: eggs, dairy, meat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CRF Nutrition (PDF p. 391)
questions.quote: Allow only protein with high biologic value

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Aluminum hydroxide (Amphojel) is given in chronic renal failure to:
questions.rationale: Phosphate binders lower hyperphosphatemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CRF Nursing (PDF p. 391)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Peritoneal dialysis outflow becomes cloudy. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Normal outflow is clear; cloudy means infection; yellow suggests bladder puncture.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peritoneal Dialysis (PDF p. 391)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before peritoneal catheter insertion, the client should:
questions.rationale: Empty bladder and bowel to prevent puncture.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peritoneal Dialysis (PDF p. 391)
questions.quote: Empty the bladder and bowel to prevent puncture

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does the nurse check patency of an AV fistula?
questions.rationale: A thrill and bruit indicate patency; absence suggests clotting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemodialysis Access (PDF p. 392)
questions.quote: Palpate for thrills, Auscultate for bruits

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are antihypertensives often held before hemodialysis?
questions.rationale: Dialysis removes fluid; combined with antihypertensives it can cause hypotension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemodialysis Nursing (PDF p. 392)
questions.quote: Antihypertensive agents must be withheld before dialysis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which pruritus measure helps a client on hemodialysis?
questions.rationale: Use bath oils, superfatted soap, lotion, and keep nails short.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemodialysis Nursing (PDF p. 392)
questions.quote: Keep nails trimmed to avoid scratching and excoriation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Under RA 7170 (Organ Donation Act of 1991), who may donate body parts by legacy?
questions.rationale: Any individual at least 18 years old and of sound mind may donate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Transplant (PDF p. 393)
questions.quote: Any individual, at least 18 years of age and of sound mind

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Under RA 7170, the donor's death must be diagnosed by:
questions.rationale: Death is diagnosed separately by two physicians who are not on the removal team.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Transplant (PDF p. 393)
questions.quote: shall be diagnosed separately by two (2) qualified physicians

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign suggests acute kidney transplant rejection?
questions.rationale: Rejection: decreased output, fever, tenderness, rising creatinine, BP, and weight.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transplant Rejection (PDF p. 394)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hyperacute kidney rejection occurs:
questions.rationale: Hyperacute rejection occurs within hours; the kidney must be removed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transplant Rejection (PDF p. 394)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most reliable test to confirm kidney transplant rejection?
questions.rationale: Renal biopsy is most reliable.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Detecting Rejection (PDF p. 394)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The major intracellular electrolyte is:
questions.rationale: ICF: potassium and phosphorus; ECF: sodium and chloride.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluids and Electrolytes (PDF p. 394)
